title: Turn your data into a table
summary: Convert a range into an Excel table and choose a table style.

steps.say: Click any cell inside your Month and Amount data, for example A3.

checks.prompt: Is a cell inside the Month and Amount data selected?

hints: Pick a cell between A1 and B7. Leave out the total and average rows.
Use the Name Box to jump to A3.
steps.why: Excel uses the selected cell to find the whole block of data.

steps.say: Select A1 to B7 by dragging from A1 down to B7.

checks.prompt: Are cells A1 to B7 highlighted, without rows 8 and 9?

hints: Leave out the total and average rows so the table holds only the data.
Type A1 colon B7 in the Name Box and press Enter.
steps.why: Selecting the exact range keeps the totals outside the table.

steps.say: Press Control T to create a table.
hints: A small Create Table window opens showing the range.
On the Home tab, click Format as Table in the Styles group and pick any style.
steps.why: Tables add filter buttons and keep formatting tidy as data grows.

steps.say: Make sure My table has headers is ticked, then click OK.

checks.prompt: Is the data now formatted as a table with banded rows and arrow buttons in the header row?

hints: The check box tells Excel that row 1 holds the column names.
Press Enter to choose OK with the keyboard.
steps.why: With headers, each column keeps its name instead of becoming data.

steps.say: On the Table Design tab, pick a different style from Table Styles.

checks.prompt: Has the table's color style changed from the default blue?

hints: Table Design appears at the top only while a cell in the table is selected.
Skip this by saying done if you like the default look. Control Z undoes a style.
steps.why: Styles make a table readable without formatting each cell.
